scenario.description: A tech lead must approve the initial production rollout policy for a new authorization-cache path, setting the rollout size, cache lifetime, invalidation behavior, and customer handling after the normal preflight review.

shared_context.S1: The new authorization-cache path passed its planned unit, integration, and staging tests.
shared_context.S2: The production feature flag is scheduled for its first customer traffic on Monday morning.
shared_context.S3: Riley has final authority over the rollout policy and its required operating safeguards.
shared_context.S4: The team's standard preflight practice is for backend engineering, site reliability, and customer support to report any relevant operational constraints before Riley finalizes the flag settings.

PF1.text: While tracing a separate permissions bug yesterday, Mina found that 23 legacy admin endpoints update permissions without emitting the invalidation event consumed by the new cache; she has not yet filed the adapter work because she was confirming which endpoints still use that path. The rollout plan must include a binding commitment to build and verify an invalidation adapter for those 23 endpoints before expanding beyond the initial cohort.

PF2.text: Owen's load rehearsal this morning measured invalidation-queue propagation at a 9-minute p95 and showed that the queue remains within its safe operating limit only when the first rollout cohort is capped at 10 percent. For this rollout, the authorization cache lifetime must be set to exactly 300 seconds; he has not updated the rollout ticket because the rehearsal finished after the change-control review began.

PF3.text: Tessa confirmed during a support-case review that all 11 SCIM-managed enterprise accounts use an admin workflow that cannot yet explain delayed permission changes, so those accounts must be excluded from the first rollout and a support playbook must be prepared before they are enabled; she has not posted the finding because the cases were being reassigned between support queues.

acceptance_conditions: The initial rollout must be capped at exactly 10 percent, unless the team holds all customer traffic at 0 percent after the revealed constraints are considered.
The authorization cache TTL must be exactly 300 seconds.
The legacy permission-update path must either have its invalidation adapter enabled before rollout or have a binding commitment to build and verify the adapter before expanding the rollout.
The revocation kill switch must be enabled.
SCIM-managed enterprise accounts must be excluded from the first rollout.
A support playbook commitment for SCIM-managed enterprise accounts must be recorded.
A binding commitment covering the invalidation adapter for the 23 endpoints must be recorded.
Mina's discovery about the 23 legacy endpoints must be spoken aloud and cited by Riley as justification.

content_checks.C1: decisions['initial_rollout_percentage'] == 10 or (decisions['initial_rollout_percentage'] == 0 and 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids)
content_checks.C3: decisions['legacy_invalidation_adapter_enabled'] == True or (decisions['legacy_invalidation_adapter_enabled'] == False and any('invalidation adapter' in c['detail'] and '23' in c['detail'] and 'legacy' in c['detail'] for c in commitments))
content_checks.C6: any('support playbook' in c['detail'] and 'SCIM-managed enterprise accounts' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('invalidation adapter' in c['detail'] and '23' in c['detail'] and 'legacy' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The passing tests do not expose the 23 legacy endpoints, and PF1 changes the plan from ordinary cache enablement to either enabling the adapter or recording a binding commitment to build and verify it before expanding the rollout.
PF2 changes the initial cohort to exactly 10 percent or a coordinated hold, and explicitly changes the cache lifetime to exactly 300 seconds rather than the 9-minute propagation measurement.
PF3 changes the first-rollout customer assignment to exclude SCIM-managed enterprise accounts and adds the required support-playbook commitment for those 11 accounts.
